name: Question 12
worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =5$ and $\sigma =10.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-18.4<X<16.7) & =P(\frac{-18.4-5}{10}<Z<\frac{16.7-5}{10}) \\  & =P(-2.34<Z<1.17)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/82e4ea3088176bbd9b03b7baa6aaa9389f21f9e9a286fa223d47bfae4252ccb6.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.34<Z<1.17) & =P(Z<1.17)-P(Z\le -2.34) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.17)-P(Z\le -2.34) \\  & =Φ(1.17)-Φ(-2.34)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-2.34) & =0.0096 \\ Φ(1.17) & =0.8790\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2.34<Z<1.17) & =Φ(1.17)-Φ(-2.34) \\  & =0.8790-0.0096 \\  & =0.8694.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(-18.4<X<16.7)=0.8694.
$$

EXPLANATION

Given a normal random variable X∼N(μ,σ2), we have

P(a<X<b)=P(a−μσ<Z<b−μσ)

where Z∼N(0,1) is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have μ=5 and σ=10.

First, we transform X into a standard normal random variable Z by z-scoring:

P(−18.4<X<16.7)=P(−18.4−510<Z<16.7−510)=P(−2.34<Z<1.17)

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

Now, we express the required probability in terms of Φ(z):

P(−2.34<Z<1.17)=P(Z<1.17)−P(Z≤−2.34)=P(Z≤1.17)−P(Z≤−2.34)=Φ(1.17)−Φ(−2.34)

From the table, we have the following:

Φ(−2.34)=0.0096Φ(1.17)=0.8790

Therefore, we have

P(−2.34<Z<1.17)=Φ(1.17)−Φ(−2.34)=0.8790−0.0096=0.8694.

Finally, we conclude that

P(−18.4<X<16.7)=0.8694.
